questions.question: School buses:

options.text: Never have ABS.
Only have ABS if students under 10 years old will ride.
May have ABS.

questions.correctAnswerText: May have ABS.
questions.explanation: Most school buses made after 1998 or 1999 must have an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS). Many older buses also have ABS.

questions.question: If a driver must leave a school bus to check if all students have boarded, the driver should:

options.text: Leave the bus running.
Turn off the bus and take the key.
Ask a student to watch the steering wheel.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn off the bus and take the key.
questions.explanation: If the driver cannot find a student who should be boarding, they must turn off the bus, take the key, and check around and under the bus for that student.

questions.question: If your bus has a manual transmission, what should you never do when crossing railroad tracks?

options.text: Change gears.
Use the brakes.
Look both ways.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change gears.
questions.explanation: Do not shift gears while crossing railroad tracks. Your bus could stall and get stuck on the tracks.

questions.question: During a basic vehicle control skills test, a look is when:

options.text: A driver checks the gauges on the dashboard.
A driver checks their blind spots.
A driver gets out and walks to the back of the vehicle to check its position.

questions.correctAnswerText: A driver gets out and walks to the back of the vehicle to check its position.
questions.explanation: A driver uses a look by opening their door, leaving their seat, and walking to the back to check where the vehicle is. During straight line backing, you may only look once. During other exercises, you may look up to two times.

questions.question: If a tornado is coming and there is no nearby building, where should students go?

options.text: To a nearby ditch.
To the closest tree.
Near a river.

questions.correctAnswerText: To a nearby ditch.
questions.explanation: If students must leave the bus during a tornado warning, take them to a building. If no building is available, take them to a nearby ditch or culvert. Avoid areas where water might flood and stay far from the bus so it will not fall on them if it tips.

questions.question: Loading and unloading a bus:

options.text: Can be dangerous for passengers.
Does not need supervision.
Should happen while refueling.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can be dangerous for passengers.
questions.explanation: More students die during bus loading and unloading than while riding the bus. School bus drivers must follow safety rules during loading and unloading.

questions.question: When parallel parking on the driver's side, you should:

options.text: Drive directly into the parking space.
Back past the space, then drive forward into it.
Drive past the space, then back into it.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive past the space, then back into it.
questions.explanation: For a parking space on your left, drive past it first. Then back into the space while keeping your vehicle close to the rear of the space. Your vehicle must be completely within the space boundaries.

questions.question: When getting out of a vehicle, a driver should:

options.text: Jump directly from the seat to the ground.
Keep at least one hand touching the vehicle.
Face the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Face the vehicle.
questions.explanation: When exiting your vehicle, you must face it and maintain three points of contact at all times. For a bus, hold the handrail. Exiting incorrectly may cause you to fail the basic vehicle control skills test.

questions.question: If your bus has a roof-mounted strobe light, use it:

options.text: When it is hard to see.
All the time.
Only at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: When it is hard to see.
questions.explanation: Use the roof strobe light when visibility is poor.

questions.question: With properly adjusted crossover mirrors, you can see all of the following except:

options.text: The right and left front tires touching the ground.
The area in front of the bus.
The tops of the right and left rear tires.

questions.correctAnswerText: The tops of the right and left rear tires.
questions.explanation: Properly adjusted crossover mirrors show the area in front of the bus from the bumper to where you can see directly. They also show the front tires touching the ground and the area from the front to the service door. They do not show the tops of the rear tires.

questions.question: When checking a fifth wheel during a pre-trip inspection, what should you look for?

options.text: A gap between the kingpin and the locking jaws.
The locking jaws fully closed around the kingpin.
Loose locking jaws.

questions.correctAnswerText: The locking jaws fully closed around the kingpin.
questions.explanation: When inspecting the fifth wheel, make sure the locking jaws are fully closed around the kingpin.

questions.question: What will the examiner score you on during the driving test?

options.text: How well you speak.
How fast you reach your destination.
Your general driving behavior.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your general driving behavior.
questions.explanation: The examiner will score you on your driving maneuvers and overall driving behavior. You must drive safely, obey all traffic signs and laws, and avoid accidents or violations.

questions.question: How should you complete an offset back/right parking maneuver?

options.text: Pull straight forward, then drive straight back.
Drive straight back, then pull forward to the left.
Pull straight forward, then back to the right.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull straight forward, then back to the right.
questions.explanation: For an offset back/right parking maneuver, pull straight forward first, then back up to the right. Your vehicle must stay within the parking space boundaries.

questions.question: What happens if your vehicle's ABS stops working?

options.text: You will have no brakes.
You will still have brakes.
You should only use the parking brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: You will still have brakes.
questions.explanation: ABS prevents wheel lockup during hard braking. If ABS breaks down, your regular brakes will still work. Drive and brake normally.

questions.question: Where should students wait to be picked up by a school bus?

options.text: At a designated bus stop.
Anywhere, and the driver will pick them up.
Wherever parents decide.

questions.correctAnswerText: At a designated bus stop.
questions.explanation: School bus drivers must load and unload students only at approved stops chosen by school district officials.

questions.question: When students board a school bus, which should the driver NOT do?

options.text: Check mirrors for students running to the bus.
Count students and make sure all have boarded.
Allow students to board in pairs.

questions.correctAnswerText: Allow students to board in pairs.
questions.explanation: The driver should count waiting students and ensure all board. Check mirrors for students running. Students must board slowly in a single-file line, not in pairs.

questions.question: If a school bus must be evacuated, which exit should passengers use?

options.text: Always the rear door.
The safest exit available.
Always the front door.

questions.correctAnswerText: The safest exit available.
questions.explanation: During an evacuation, the driver must quickly decide which exit is safest for passengers to use.

questions.question: What should you do when crossing railroad tracks during the driving test?

options.text: Pass a slow vehicle on the tracks.
Get out and check for a train.
Do not change gears while on the tracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not change gears while on the tracks.
questions.explanation: Do not stop, change gears, pass vehicles, or change lanes while any part of your vehicle is on railroad tracks.

questions.question: As students exit a school bus, what should the driver watch for?

options.text: Students leaving in pairs.
Students getting caught on the handrail or door.
Students talking while exiting.

questions.correctAnswerText: Students getting caught on the handrail or door.
questions.explanation: Students can be injured if their clothing or bodies get caught on a handrail or door while exiting. The driver must watch carefully to make sure all students exit safely.

questions.question: Where is the overhead rearview mirror located on a school bus?

options.text: On the right side of the bus.
On the steering wheel.
Above the windshield inside the bus.

questions.correctAnswerText: Above the windshield inside the bus.
questions.explanation: The overhead inside rearview mirror is mounted above the windshield on the driver's side. Use it to monitor students inside the bus.
